intervals.label: water-fill commissioning
intervals.locator: arXiv:2104.11687 (JINST 16 P08059), description of the three operating phases
intervals.note: The collaboration's detector paper dates the water phase (the acrylic vessel filled with 905 t of ultrapure water, run as a water Cherenkov detector) to May 2017 - July 2019; the paper says the purpose of the water fill was to re-commission the detector and mitigate radon ingress.
intervals.quote: The water phase was used to collect physics data by operating SNO+ as a water Cherenkov detector from May 2017 to July 2019 while filled with 905 tonnes of UPW.

end.display: by April 2026 (leak repair under way); onset not sourced

intervals.label: liquid-scintillator phase
intervals.note: Start is taken as May 2022, the date of the SNOLAB news item announcing the scintillator fill and PPO loading complete; earlier filling steps are not dated here. The acrylic-vessel leak repair was under way by April 2026 (LIP slide: "lowering water now to repair"); onset date not sourced.
intervals.quote: The SNO+ experiment completes scintillator fill and PPO loading May 17, 2022 ... has completed the liquid scintillator detector fill and PPO loading marking a huge milestone for the experiment.

intervals.label: acrylic vessel leak repair
intervals.note: LIP Advisory Committee slide (27-28 April 2026, J. Maneira): "Acrylic Vessel Repairs: leak in AV, height identified, lowering water now to repair, autumn restart". SNOLAB report of 26 May 2026 has a slide 'SNO+ Cavity Access for Repairs' (rope-access team, boat in the cavity, "No damage to the neck. AV was not stuck", "Installing lights"; photo of the cavity with the water level lowered), so the repair was under way in spring 2026. No source gives the day the scintillator data-taking stopped (the April 2026 reactor analysis, arXiv:2604.05746, uses data "between May 2022 and July 2025", which is an analysis cut, not an end of running), so the start is 'by April 2026' at month precision, approximate. The restart is a plan: 'autumn restart' (autumn 2026 = September-November, middle month 2026-10); the slide does not say what restarts (scintillator data-taking or water fill) and no source dated after 26 May 2026 reports it, so the shutdown is kept at 2026-10-25 and is unconfirmed.
intervals.quote: leak in AV, height identified, lowering water now to repair, autumn restart

start.display: by April 2026 (leak repair under way); onset not sourced

name: SNO+ detector
notes: Modelled as a distinct detector record from detector:sno despite sharing the same physical acrylic vessel/cavern, because the target medium and physics program changed materially (heavy water -> water -> liquid scintillator, eventually tellurium-loaded); see experiment:sno-plus.lineage (`upgrade_of` experiment:sno).

placements.locator: arXiv:2104.11687 (JINST 16 P08059), description of the three operating phases
placements.note: Placed at site:snolab-underground-lab, the same cavern as experiment:sno. Start is the year of the first water fill (May 2017), a lower bound for when this detector configuration was in place.
placements.quote: In the first operating phase of the experiment, or “water phase”, the SNO+ detector was initially filled with light water (H2O) in May 2017.

target_mass.note: The SNO+ collaboration's About page gives 780 tonnes of liquid scintillator in the acrylic vessel; SNOLAB's May 2022 news item says the same after the fill.
target_mass.quote: The heart of the SNO+ detector is a 12m diameter acrylic sphere filled with 780 tonnes of liquid scintillator

summary.plain: The same 12-metre acrylic ball that once held SNO's heavy water, now filled with liquid scintillator, watching for solar neutrinos, reactor antineutrinos, and a hoped-for rare nuclear decay.
summary.technical: SNO's original acrylic vessel and PMT support structure, water-filled 2017-2019 for commissioning, then filled with 780 t of LAB+PPO liquid scintillator from 2022; a future phase will load natural tellurium for a 0νββ search.

technology.note: The SNO+ About page states that the acrylic sphere, PMTs and PMT support structure are from the original SNO experiment and that the detector was previously filled with ultrapure water. The planned tellurium loading is recorded on experiment:sno-plus (LIP Advisory Committee slide), not repeated here.
technology.quote: a 12m diameter acrylic sphere filled with 780 tonnes of liquid scintillator ... The acrylic sphere, PMTs and PMT support structure were from the original SNO Experiment. ... Previously, the detector was filled with ultrapure water and operated as a water Cherenkov detector.
technology.value: The original SNO 12 m acrylic vessel, photomultiplier tubes and PMT support structure, filled first with ultrapure water and now with liquid scintillator
